chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Dynamics in big bands then and now
summary: Ellington, Miller and Hopkins used dynamics; modern bands blow open and sound monotonous.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: You know, I hadn't thought about it. But it's really what Claude Hopkins did to that band. Because that was a very soft band, wasn't it, for a long time.
Oh yeah. They played...
Everything was very (?) and was light.

Well, in those days, too, they knew how...the dynamic... The bands used dynamics much more extensively. Though when the Bebop Era came, or something like that, these combos were playing one extensive line, they'd play a lot of runs and everything -- the innovation was harmonic. But they always played on one tone level. They didn't use dynamics like in the old days.
Ramirez - 173
Big bands, too... But then in later years, when they did eight brass and everything...
Yeah. But you have a contrast in sound -- the sound level.
But you know, today, in those big bands, they don't... I mean, everybody talks about Ellington, but nobody copies his conception of dynamics!

Oh, all of them used dynamics. Glenn Miller used dynamics. They played a (?). But later on, you know... All bands... And even the sound of let's say Count Basie; the brass section would play in unison often with the open horn. I daresay even... I guess Dizzy Gillespie reaching for a contrast, eventually, he'll put a mute in his horn.

But the big bands that you hear around today mostly, they don't use mutes, and they've really... Their concept of dynamic coloring and so forth is to alternate a brass section with a flute solo or something like that. But that's what we're talking about, is it.
No. You're talking about an instrumental difference. I'm talking about a...
Sort of like a volume...
Yeah, a difference in volumes.
Yeah.
Ramirez - 174
I mean, you can use woodwinds and just, you know, you have different tones or different tone colors, like that. But yeah, I'm speaking about the dynamics of these...

I am, too. But what I meant was that I hear a lot of these big bands that record... Now, Basie still uses these mutes, and they will still go down and come up. But most of these bands are blowing open...
Today.
Yeah.
I see what you mean. You're talking about the general trend nowadays.
It gets very boring, you know.
Yes, it's boring if you hear one sound. It's like listening to a vocalist that has no frequency in their...
